text: The search team evaluated a revised cache key on the staging cluster during Tuesday's routine performance window. The team used the same synthetic catalog snapshot for both runs and recorded latency at the service boundary. The change reduced median lookup latency by 18% in that staging test. This result covers only the synthetic catalog and the staging traffic profile. Production traffic has not been tested. Deploy only after a production-shaped load test passes. The improvement was most visible during a repeated-query segment, and the team did not change the storage engine or the number of replicas between the two runs. The dashboard contains the traces under the performance-window label, and the query generator configuration is stored with the staging job. A separate memory panel showed a higher peak after the change, but the measurement was too noisy for the team to draw a conclusion from it. The on-call engineer requested a short handoff so the next shift would know which checks had already been run. The change is behind a configuration flag in the staging environment. The flag name and routine maintenance notes are documented in the internal test ticket. No production rollout window has been reserved.

text: The device team compared a revised battery indicator with the existing indicator on a bench using twelve identical evaluation boards. The revised indicator reported the remaining charge more accurately during the steady-load portion of the bench test. During the pulse-load portion, its error was larger than the existing indicator's error. The team has not established whether either result applies to aged batteries. Do not enable the revision for field units until the pulse-load error is investigated and the test owner signs off. The boards all used cells from the same shipment, and the test equipment logged voltage and current at the same sampling interval for both versions. The team alternated the order of the versions between boards to reduce order effects. The raw measurements and calibration notes are stored with the bench report. One board was removed before comparison because a connector failed; the twelve boards reported above all completed both portions. The support team asked for a concise handoff before the next bench session. A display color change was considered separately and was not part of this comparison. The next engineer should find the pulse-load script in the test folder and note any equipment changes in the bench log.
